title: Lipids in microalgae quantitation
author: Yingyu Hu
materials: Preparation of standard Glyceryl tripalmitate Contributed by users
Discard the remaining extract solution into waste tank.
Determine the subsampling method for the remaining replicates
For samples, subsample following the preliminary test.
For samples: Lipids_{ug/filter} =Lipids_{ug}*4/2 For blanks: Lipids_{ug/filter} =Lipids_{ug}*5/4.5

steps.title: Prepare GTP Primary Standard Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a glyceryl tripalmitate (GTP) primary standard solution with a concentration of approximately 1 mg/mL.

substeps.instruction: Place frozen GTP in a vacuum desiccator with a loose cap until it warms to room temperature.
Weigh approximately 1-2 mg of GTP and transfer it to a clear vial, logging the actual weight.
Dissolve the GTP in chloroform to achieve a concentration of about 1 mg/mL and gently vortex.

steps.title: Prepare Working Standards
steps.instruction: Create a series of working standards in 12 mL vials by adding specific volumes of the GTP primary standard.

substeps.instruction: For 5 µg/vial: Add 5 µL primary standard to a clear vial.
For 10 µg/vial: Add 10 µL primary standard to a clear vial.
For 20 µg/vial: Add 20 µL primary standard to a clear vial.
For 40 µg/vial: Add 40 µL primary standard to an amber vial (or clear vial as per conflicting text).
For 80 µg/vial: Add 80 µL primary standard to a clear vial.
For 100 µg/vial: Add 100 µL primary standard to a clear vial.
For 120 µg/vial: Add 2 x 60 µL primary standard to a clear vial using a chloroform-rinsed 100 µL glass syringe.
For 160 µg/vial: Add 2 x 80 µL primary standard to a clear vial using a chloroform-rinsed 100 µL glass syringe.
For 200 µg/vial: Add 2 x 100 µL primary standard to a clear vial using a chloroform-rinsed 100 µL glass syringe.
For 240 µg/vial: Add 3 x 80 µL primary standard to a clear vial using a chloroform-rinsed 100 µL glass syringe.
For 300 µg/vial: Add 3 x 100 µL primary standard to a clear vial using a chloroform-rinsed 100 µL glass syringe.
Dry all working standards at room temperature under an N2 gas stream (<2 psi).

steps.title: Prepare Acid-Dichromate Reagent
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.15% (w/w) potassium dichromate in concentrated sulfuric acid reagent.

substeps.instruction: Estimate total volume of potassium dichromate required: V = 0.5 * (Number of standards + standard blanks + samples using 0.5 mL) + 0.2 * (Number of sample blanks + samples using 0.2 mL).
Transfer concentrated sulfuric acid to a 95% ethanol-rinsed and air-dried glass reagent bottle.
Weigh an empty, 95% ethanol-rinsed and air-dried glass reagent bottle and tare the balance.
Use a 5 mL serological pipet to transfer concentrated sulfuric acid into the vial (volume should be several mL more than the estimate); record the weight of the acid.
Calculate the required weight of potassium dichromate: Weight = (Weight of sulfuric acid) * (0.15 / 99.85).
Weigh the potassium dichromate and dissolve it into the concentrated sulfuric acid; cap and vortex until completely dissolved.

steps.title: Process Microalgae Samples
steps.instruction: Extract and prepare microalgae samples for assay, including sample blanks.

substeps.instruction: For sample blanks: Add 5 mL chloroform, transfer 4.5 mL to a new vial, discard the remainder, and dry the extract in the new vial.
For samples: Add 5 mL chloroform to the dried extract.
Transfer 4.5 mL into a new vial and dry for assay.
Alternatively, for specific sample concentrations: Add 4 mL chloroform to the dried sample extract, transfer 2 mL into a new vial, and dry for assay.
Store any remaining extract at -80 °C for phospholipids assay.

steps.title: Perform Dichromate Reaction
steps.instruction: React the standards and samples with the acid-dichromate reagent in a boiling water bath.

substeps.instruction: Label two 12 mL vials as '+ Blank' (absorbance reference) and '- Blank' (0 µg GTP).
Prepare a boiling water bath on a hot plate with a vial rack.
Add 0.5 mL of acid-dichromate reagent to standards, +Blank, -Blank, and designated samples using a 5 mL serological pipet (fill to 4 mL, dispense 0.5 mL).
Add 0.2 mL of acid-dichromate reagent to sample blanks and designated samples using a 5 mL serological pipet (fill to 4 mL, dispense 0.2 mL).
Cap and vortex all vials immediately.
Keep reaction vials in the boiling water bath for 15 minutes.
Cool vials to room temperature in a fume hood.

steps.title: Stop Reaction and Prepare for Measurement
steps.instruction: Quench the reaction with MilliQ water and sodium sulphite.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.2 g/mL sodium sulphite solution by dissolving 0.2 g sodium sulphite in 1 mL MilliQ water (or 0.4 g in 2 mL) in a microtube and vortexing.
Add 1.125 mL MilliQ (1 mL + 125 µL) to vials that reacted with 0.5 mL dichromate; cap and vortex immediately.
Add 450 µL MilliQ to vials that reacted with 0.2 mL dichromate; cap and vortex immediately.
Cool vials to room temperature.
Add 25 µL of the 0.2 g/mL sodium sulphite solution to the '+Blank' vial and vortex.

steps.title: Quantify Lipids
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance and calculate lipid mass using a standard curve.

substeps.instruction: Load 200 µL of reactant into a microtiter plate using reverse pipetting.
Subtract the absorbance of the '+Blank' from the absorbance of the standards.
Plot absorbance versus mass of GTP (µg) to create a standard curve.
Calculate the mass of lipids in samples: GTP_{ug} = (Abs - intercept) / slope.
Adjust for dichromate volume: Lipids_{ug} = GTP_{ug} * (0.5 / V_{dichromate}).

Calculate final lipid content per filter: Lipids_{ug/filter} = (V1 / V2) * Lipids_{ug}, where V1 is the volume of chloroform added to the dried extract and V2 is the volume of extract used in the assay.
